title: Zoho Analytics alternatives (2026): 8 BI tools compared on live queries, AI, row-level security, and pricing
summary: Power BI, Metabase, Data Studio, Tableau, ThoughtSpot, Sigma, Domo, and Basedash compared as Zoho Analytics alternatives on live queries, AI, RLS, and price.
body_markdown:
The most common Zoho Analytics alternatives in 2026 are Microsoft Power BI for Microsoft 365 companies, Metabase for a low-cost or self-hosted option, Google Data Studio (formerly Looker Studio) for free reporting on Google data, Tableau for analyst-led visualization, ThoughtSpot and Basedash for teams that want to ask questions in plain English, Sigma for live analysis on a cloud warehouse, and Domo for connector breadth with unlimited users. Zoho Analytics stays hard to beat on entry price, so most teams switch because they need live warehouse queries on every plan, SCIM provisioning, or AI that works on their own database rather than imported copies. Every price below was checked on the vendor’s official page on October 7, 2026.


## Why teams look for a Zoho Analytics alternative


Zoho Analytics is a capable, inexpensive BI tool. As of October 2026, its[pricing page](https://www.zoho.com/analytics/pricing.html) lists Basic at $24 per month (2 users, 0.5 million rows), Standard at $48 (5 users, 1 million rows), Premium at $115 (15 users, 5 million rows), and Enterprise at $455 (50 users, 50 million rows), all billed annually, with a free plan for 2 users and 10,000 rows. It ships anomaly detection, an MCP server, and native connectors for Zoho CRM and Zoho Books on every plan. Teams usually start comparing alternatives for one of five reasons.


**Live queries need Premium or Enterprise.** The[Live Connect documentation](https://www.zoho.com/analytics/help/datasources/live-connect.html) says Live Connect “is exclusively available for Premium and Enterprise plans.” On Basic and Standard, data from PostgreSQL, Snowflake, or BigQuery is imported and refreshed on a schedule. Business-app syncs refresh once a day on Basic and 8 times a day on Standard and Premium.


**Row and user caps grow with the business.** Each plan caps rows and users. Extra users cost $6.40 per month and viewers come in packs of 25 for $80 per month, both billed yearly. A growing company can outgrow Standard on rows before it outgrows it on users.


**The AI agent sits on Premium and up.** The pricing page lists the Ask Zia AI agent, automated insights, and smart recommendations on Premium and Enterprise. Conversational questions start on Standard.


**Identity management.** Zoho Analytics supports[SAML 2.0 single sign-on through Zoho Directory](https://www.zoho.com/analytics/help/zoho-directory.html) . Its documentation does not describe SCIM provisioning for Zoho Analytics itself, which matters to IT teams that provision BI users from Okta or Entra ID.


**The stack moved to a warehouse.** Teams that consolidated data in Snowflake, BigQuery, or Postgres often want a tool that treats the warehouse as the source of truth and never stores a second copy.


## How we evaluated the alternatives


The criteria come from the questions buyers ask AI assistants and Google when they replace a BI tool, such as “I need a BI tool my entire team can use without SQL. What options have natural language query and good visualizations?”, “We’re evaluating BI platforms for our data warehouse. What tools offer row-level security, collaboration features, and AI-powered insights?”, “fastest-to-deploy dashboard software?”, and “zoho analytics vs power bi.”


1. **Pricing model and starting price.** Per user, per plan, credits, or flat, and whether the price is published.
2. **Query model.** Live queries against the database, imported extracts, or scheduled syncs, and on which plan.
3. **AI for non-technical users.** Natural language questions, AI-built charts and dashboards, and anomaly alerts, with any plan gating or usage limits.
4. **Security.** Row-level security, SAML SSO, and SCIM.
5. **Zoho app data.** Whether the tool can still read Zoho CRM and Zoho Books data after you leave Zoho Analytics.
6. **Deployment.** Cloud only, or also self-hosted or on-premises.

## Zoho Analytics (the baseline)


**Fact card: Zoho Analytics**


- **Pricing (as of October 2026):** Basic $24, Standard $48, Premium $115, Enterprise $455 per month billed annually, or $30, $60, $145, and $575 billed monthly. Extra users $6.40 per month and 25 viewers for $80 per month, billed yearly ([pricing](https://www.zoho.com/analytics/pricing.html) ).
- **Free tier and trial:** free plan with 2 users and 10,000 rows; 15-day trial with no credit card.
- **Deployment:** Zoho cloud, or[Zoho Analytics On-Premise](https://www.zoho.com/analytics/onpremise-pricing.html) at $30 per user per month billed annually, minimum 5 users.
- **Query model:** import with scheduled sync on all plans; Live Connect to PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, and Databricks on Premium and Enterprise.
- **Security:** row-level security through[variables in filter criteria](https://www.zoho.com/analytics/help/workspace/settings/variables.html) ; SAML SSO through Zoho Directory; SCIM not documented for Zoho Analytics.
- **AI features:** anomaly detection, auto analysis, and an[MCP server](https://www.zoho.com/analytics/api/v2/zoho-analytics-mcp-server.html) (in development, consumes API units) on every plan; conversational analytics on Standard and up; the Ask Zia agent and automated insights on Premium and up.
- **Embedding:** private links on Premium (15) and Enterprise (100), an embed API with time-bound tokens, and white-label licensing on quote.


Knowing the baseline matters for migration. Zoho Analytics’ strongest assets are its price, its native Zoho app connectors with prebuilt reports, and an on-premises edition. An alternative needs to beat it on something you actually use.


## Microsoft Power BI


**Best for:** companies on Microsoft 365 and Entra ID that want the lowest per-user price from a major vendor.


Power BI is the most common Zoho Analytics comparison (“zoho analytics vs power bi” is one of the top searches in the category). Per user, Power BI Pro and Zoho Analytics Basic or Standard land in a similar range for small teams, but Power BI charges every person who shares or views content, while Zoho Analytics plans include a set number of users.


**Fact card: Microsoft Power BI**


- **Pricing (as of October 2026):** Free account for personal use; Pro $14 per user per month and Premium Per User $24, paid yearly ([pricing](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/products/power-bi/pricing) ). Free users can view shared content only on F64 or P1 capacity and above.
- **Deployment:** Power BI service, or[Power BI Report Server](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/report-server/get-started) on-premises through Fabric F64+ reservations or SQL Server Enterprise licensing.
- **Query model:** import or DirectQuery for[PostgreSQL](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-query/connectors/postgresql) ,[Snowflake](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-query/connectors/snowflake) , and[BigQuery](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-query/connectors/google-bigquery) ; the[MySQL connector](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-query/connectors/mysql-database) is import only. Imported models refresh up to[8 times a day on Pro and 48 on PPU](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/connect-data/refresh-data) .
- **Security:**[row-level security](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/security/service-admin-row-level-security) with DAX roles, which applies to Viewers only, not workspace Admins, Members, or Contributors; identity through Microsoft Entra ID.
- **AI features:**[Copilot](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/create-reports/copilot-introduction) requires paid Fabric F2 or Premium P1 capacity, and a Pro or PPU license alone is not enough. Q&A is being retired in February 2027.
- **Zoho data:** a native Zoho Creator connector; no Zoho CRM or Zoho Books connector in the[connector list](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-query/connectors/) .
- **Not ideal for:** teams that want natural language AI without buying Fabric capacity, or teams that want free viewers on a small deployment.


**Tradeoffs:** Power BI has the widest ecosystem in this list, but its AI is priced separately from its seats. Price Copilot as a Fabric capacity line item before comparing it to Zoho’s Ask Zia, which is included in Premium.


## Metabase


**Best for:** teams with an engineer who want the cheapest path to dashboards, with an open-source or self-hosted option.


**Fact card: Metabase**


- **Pricing (as of October 2026):** Open Source free; Starter $100 per month with 5 users included, then $6 per user (cloud only); Pro $575 per month with 10 users included, then $12 per user; Enterprise from $20,000 per year. Yearly billing saves 10% ([pricing](https://www.metabase.com/pricing/) ). 14-day trial.
- **Deployment:** Metabase Cloud or self-hosted with Docker or a JAR file; air-gapped on Enterprise.
- **Query model:** live queries against PostgreSQL, MySQL, Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, Databricks, and other[official drivers](https://www.metabase.com/docs/latest/databases/connecting) ; result caching on Pro and Enterprise.
- **Security:**[row and column security](https://www.metabase.com/docs/latest/permissions/row-and-column-security) , SAML SSO, and SCIM on Pro and Enterprise.
- **AI features:**[Metabot](https://www.metabase.com/docs/latest/ai/metabot) creates charts from natural language, writes SQL, and fixes query errors on every plan. Metabase’s AI service costs $3.75 per million tokens after the first million, or you bring your own key. An MCP server is on every plan.
- **Embedding:** guest embeds on every plan; the Modular embedding SDK for React on Pro and Enterprise.
- **Zoho data:** no Zoho connector; you need an ETL tool to land Zoho CRM data in a database first.
- **Not ideal for:** teams with no one to host it or model tables, or teams that need row-level security on the $100 Starter plan.


**Tradeoffs:** Metabase’s free tier is genuinely free, and Starter costs about what Zoho Analytics Premium costs for a small team. The jump to Pro for row-level security and SSO is steep, so price Pro if either is a requirement.


## Google Data Studio (formerly Looker Studio)


**Best for:** small teams whose data lives in Google Sheets, Google Ads, Google Analytics, or BigQuery and who want free reports.


Google renamed Looker Studio back to[Data Studio in April 2026](https://docs.cloud.google.com/data-studio/welcome) . It is the only hosted tool in this list that is free for any number of creators and viewers.


**Fact card: Data Studio**


- **Pricing (as of October 2026):** free for creators and viewers; Data Studio Pro $9 per user per project per month, billed monthly for every license ([pricing](https://cloud.google.com/data-studio) ). 30-day Pro trial.
- **Deployment:** Google-hosted only.
- **Query model:** live queries with a[data freshness](https://docs.cloud.google.com/data-studio/manage-data-freshness) cache. Database connectors refresh every 1 minute to 12 hours (12 hours by default); Google Ads and Analytics are fixed at 12 hours. Google-built connectors cover BigQuery, PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, and Redshift; Snowflake and Databricks need partner connectors.
- **Security:** row-level security through[filter by email address](https://docs.cloud.google.com/data-studio/filter-by-email-address) on the free tier; sign-in uses Google accounts, and SAML and SCIM are not documented.
- **AI features:**[Conversational Analytics](https://docs.cloud.google.com/data-studio/conversational-analytics-overview) for all users on BigQuery data agents; Gemini-generated calculated fields and slide exports on Pro.
- **Embedding:** iframe embeds that always show the Data Studio watermark.
- **Zoho data:** no Google-built Zoho connector; partner connectors exist, such as a Zoho CRM connector listed on Zoho Marketplace.
- **Not ideal for:** teams that need scheduled reports at volume (one schedule per report on the free tier) or alerts, which are Pro only.


**Tradeoffs:** Data Studio removes the license budget but adds connector work for anything outside Google. Teams leaving Zoho for cost reasons should check how they will pull Zoho CRM data before committing.


## Tableau


**Best for:** analyst teams that build complex visualizations and want the deepest charting control.


**Fact card: Tableau**


- **Pricing (as of October 2026):** Standard edition Creator $75, Explorer $42, and Viewer $15 per user per month; Enterprise edition $115, $70, and $35; all billed annually ([pricing](https://www.tableau.com/pricing/cloud) ). Tableau Cloud+ and the Tableau+ Bundle are quote only. Free trial.
- **Deployment:** Tableau Cloud, or Tableau Server on-premises or in your cloud.
- **Query model:**[live connections or extracts](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-gb/to_publish.htm) for PostgreSQL, MySQL, Snowflake, BigQuery, and others; Tableau Bridge for private networks.
- **Security:** user filters in every edition; centralized data policies need Data Management, which is included in Enterprise ([RLS options](https://help.tableau.com/current/server/en-us/rls_options_overview.htm) ). SAML and OIDC SSO, plus[SCIM](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/scim_config_online.htm) with Entra ID, Okta, OneLogin, and PingFederate.
- **AI features:** Tableau Pulse metric digests on every Cloud edition; Tableau Agent only on Cloud+ and Tableau+.
- **Embedding:** Embedding API v3 with connected-app JWTs; a usage-based embedded license billed by analytical impressions.
- **Zoho data:** no native Zoho CRM or Zoho Books connector.
- **Not ideal for:** small teams that want natural language AI at a published price, or teams that want monthly billing.


**Tradeoffs:** A 5-person team on Tableau Creator licenses pays $375 per month before any viewers, more than three times Zoho Analytics Premium for 15 users. Tableau earns that price when analysts need its visualization depth.


## ThoughtSpot


**Best for:** teams that want search-style and agent-style questions in plain English as the main way non-technical users explore data.


**Fact card: ThoughtSpot**


- **Pricing (as of October 2026):** Essentials from $25 per user per month for 5 to 50 users and 25 million rows; Pro from $50 per user per month for up to 1,000 users and 250 million rows; a usage-based Pro option from $0.10 per credit; Enterprise custom. All billed annually ([pricing](https://www.thoughtspot.com/pricing) ). 14-day trial, no credit card.
- **Deployment:** ThoughtSpot Cloud or ThoughtSpot Software on-premises.
- **Query model:**[live queries by default](https://docs.thoughtspot.com/cloud/latest/connections) against Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, Databricks, PostgreSQL, MySQL, and others; an in-memory cache is an add-on.
- **Security:** row-level security on every plan; SAML SSO on Pro and Enterprise; SCIM supported.
- **AI features:**[Spotter](https://docs.thoughtspot.com/cloud/latest/spotter) AI analyst on Pro and Enterprise, capped at 25 queries per user per month on per-user Pro, with unlimited Spotter as an add-on;[KPI monitor](https://docs.thoughtspot.com/cloud/latest/monitor) anomaly and threshold alerts on all plans; the MCP server is an Enterprise add-on.
- **Zoho data:** no Zoho source connector, though ThoughtSpot can[sync results out to Zoho CRM](https://docs.thoughtspot.com/cloud/latest/sync-zoho) .
- **Not ideal for:** teams that want Spotter on the entry plan, since Essentials does not include it.


**Tradeoffs:** ThoughtSpot’s natural language search is one of the most complete in this list, and its answer quality depends on a well-modeled data layer. Check whether 25 Spotter queries per user per month covers your heaviest users.


## Sigma


**Best for:** teams on Snowflake, Databricks, or BigQuery that want spreadsheet-style analysis directly on live warehouse data.


**Fact card: Sigma**


- **Pricing (as of October 2026):** quote only; licenses come in View, Act, Analyze, and Build tiers priced by your account executive ([license overview](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/account-type-and-license-overview) ). 7-day free trial.
- **Deployment:** SaaS on AWS, Azure, or GCP.
- **Query model:** live SQL against the connected platform. Sigma[does not store your data](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/caching-and-data-freshness) and supports Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery, Redshift, PostgreSQL, MySQL, and others.
- **Security:**[row-level security](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/set-up-row-level-security) and column-level security; SAML SSO; SCIM, which requires SAML.
- **AI features:**[Sigma Assistant](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/ask-natural-language-queries-with-assistant) answers natural language questions using an AI provider you configure; Sigma agents run inside workbooks and will use consumption credits from November 1, 2026.
- **Embedding:** secure embeds, a premium feature, and an Embed SDK for React.
- **Zoho data:** no Zoho connector; Zoho data has to reach your warehouse first.
- **Not ideal for:** teams without a cloud warehouse, or teams that want a published price.


**Tradeoffs:** Sigma moves compute to your warehouse, so warehouse costs become part of the BI bill. It suits companies that already left Zoho-style imports behind and run everything through Snowflake or Databricks.


## Domo


**Best for:** companies that want many prebuilt connectors, including Zoho CRM, and unlimited users on a consumption contract.


Domo is now part of Progress Software, which[completed its acquisition](https://domo-webflow.domo.com/news/press/progress-software-completes-acquisition-of-domos-ai-and-data-platform-business) of Domo’s platform business in September 2026. The[Domo acquisition guide](https://www.basedash.com/blog/domo-acquired-by-progress-software-alternatives) covers what changed.


**Fact card: Domo**


- **Pricing (as of October 2026):** credit-based consumption with unlimited users; custom pricing through sales ([pricing](https://www.domo.com/pricing) ). 30-day free trial, no credit card.
- **Deployment:** Domo cloud; the Workbench agent brings in on-premises data.
- **Query model:** connectors import data into Domo;[Cloud Integrations](https://www.domo.com/docs/s/article/4412849158167) read live from Snowflake and BigQuery with pushdown, and from PostgreSQL and MySQL read-only.
- **Security:** row policies and column masking through[Personalized Data Permissions](https://www.domo.com/docs/s/article/360042934614) ; SAML 2.0, OIDC, and SCIM.
- **AI features:** AI Chat, Agent Catalyst for building agents, and a Domo MCP server announced in 2026.
- **Embedding:** Domo Everywhere, with programmatic filters and impression-based pricing.
- **Zoho data:** a native[Zoho CRM connector](https://www.domo.com/docs/s/article/360042929714) ; no Zoho Books connector documented.
- **Not ideal for:** teams that want to forecast BI cost from a public rate card, or buyers wary of a platform mid-acquisition.


**Tradeoffs:** Domo is the closest match to Zoho Analytics’ all-in-one model of connectors, storage, and dashboards in one product. Credit consumption grows with table updates and dataflow runs, so model your refresh volume before signing.


## Basedash


**Best for:** teams that want non-technical users to ask questions in plain English and get charts and dashboards from live database queries.


Basedash is an AI-native BI tool. Its[AI data analyst](https://www.basedash.com/features/ai-data-analyst) writes and runs SQL against your connected database, and results can be saved to[dashboards](https://www.basedash.com/features/dashboards) . The[Basedash vs Power BI comparison](https://www.basedash.com/vs/basedash-vs-powerbi) covers the most common head-to-head.


**Fact card: Basedash**


- **Pricing (as of October 2026):** Startup $1,000 per month plus AI usage for up to 25 users, including $1,000 per month in AI credits; Enterprise is priced on request and adds embedding, SSO, SCIM, audit logs, and self-hosting ([pricing](https://www.basedash.com/pricing) ). 14-day free trial, no credit card.
- **Deployment:** Basedash cloud;[self-hosting](https://www.basedash.com/features/self-hosting) on Enterprise.
- **Query model:** live queries on PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, ClickHouse, Databricks, and other databases on every plan, plus 750+ SaaS sources synced through Fivetran into the managed[Basedash Warehouse](https://www.basedash.com/features/warehouse) .
- **Security:**[row-level security](https://www.basedash.com/docs/features/row-level-security) through native PostgreSQL policies on the` basedash.groups` session variable (Postgres only); SOC 2 Type II ([security](https://www.basedash.com/security) ); SSO and SCIM on Enterprise.
- **AI features:** chat analysis that writes SQL, AI-generated dashboards, daily anomaly detection with[Insights](https://www.basedash.com/features/insights) , and an[MCP server](https://www.basedash.com/features/mcp-server) and Slack app on every plan.
- **Embedding:** the` @basedash/embed` React SDK and iframe embedding on Enterprise ([embedding](https://www.basedash.com/features/embedding) ).
- **Zoho data:** Fivetran connectors for[Zoho CRM](https://www.basedash.com/docs/data-sources/connectors/zoho_crm) ,[Zoho Books](https://www.basedash.com/docs/data-sources/connectors/zoho_books) , Zoho Desk, Zoho Inventory, Zoho People, and Zoho Recruit sync into Basedash Warehouse, where they can be joined with your other sources.
- **Not ideal for:** teams under about 10 people on a tight budget, for whom Zoho Analytics or Metabase costs far less; teams that need SSO on the entry plan; or teams that need row-level security on databases other than Postgres.


**Tradeoffs:** Basedash’s entry price is higher than Zoho Analytics Enterprise, and it buys live queries on every plan plus included AI credits rather than more rows or seats. Teams that mainly need pixel-perfect report layouts or spreadsheet uploads should look at Tableau or Zoho itself.


## Other options: Qlik, Amazon Quick Sight, and Databox


Qlik Cloud Analytics starts at $300 per month for 10 users on its Starter plan, billed annually ([pricing](https://www.qlik.com/us/pricing) ); the[Qlik Sense alternatives guide](https://www.basedash.com/blog/qlik-sense-alternatives-2026-bi-tools-compared) compares it in detail. Amazon Quick Sight suits AWS-native companies with per-reader pricing. Databox and Geckoboard fit KPI dashboards for small teams; the[small business dashboard software comparison](https://www.basedash.com/blog/best-dashboard-software-for-small-businesses-compared-2026) covers them next to Zoho Analytics.


## How to keep Zoho CRM and Zoho Books data after you leave Zoho Analytics


Zoho Analytics syncs Zoho CRM in near real time and ships prebuilt reports for Zoho apps. That is the hardest thing to replace. As of October 2026, the alternatives fall into three groups:


- **Native connector:** Domo has a native Zoho CRM connector. Power BI has a native Zoho Creator connector only.
- **Managed sync included:** Basedash syncs Zoho CRM, Zoho Books, and four other Zoho apps through Fivetran into its managed warehouse.
- **Bring your own pipeline:** Metabase, Tableau, ThoughtSpot, and Sigma have no Zoho connector, so Zoho data must land in a database or warehouse first through an ETL tool. Data Studio relies on partner connectors.


If Zoho apps are your main data source and you have no warehouse, staying on Zoho Analytics or choosing Domo or Basedash avoids building that pipeline.


## Which Zoho Analytics alternative should you choose?


- **Your team needs natural language questions without writing SQL:** ThoughtSpot (Spotter on Pro), Basedash (on every plan), or Metabase (Metabot on every plan). Power BI Copilot needs Fabric capacity.
- **You want the fastest setup for a small team:** Data Studio for Google data, Metabase Cloud Starter for a database, or Basedash if you want AI-built dashboards from a database connection.
- **You need row-level security, SSO, and SCIM for a warehouse rollout:** Tableau Enterprise, Sigma, Domo, Metabase Pro, or Basedash Enterprise. The[row-level security comparison](https://www.basedash.com/blog/best-bi-tools-for-row-level-security-compared-2026) covers setup differences.
- **You run on Microsoft 365:** Power BI.
- **You need on-premises deployment, as Zoho Analytics On-Premise offers:** Power BI Report Server, Tableau Server, ThoughtSpot Software, Metabase self-hosted, or Basedash Enterprise.
- **You want unlimited users on one contract:** Domo, or Metabase Open Source if you can host it.
- **You want anomaly alerts emailed to stakeholders:** ThoughtSpot KPI monitor, Basedash Insights, or Metabase alerts. Zoho Analytics includes anomaly detection on every plan, so check this is a real gap first.


For a plan-by-plan view of prices and AI costs across these tools, see the[BI tool pricing reference](https://www.basedash.com/blog/bi-tool-pricing-plans-seat-limits-and-ai-costs-2026) .


## Frequently asked questions


### What are the best Zoho Analytics alternatives?


The most common replacements are Power BI for Microsoft-centric companies, Metabase for low-cost or self-hosted analytics, Data Studio for free reporting on Google data, Tableau for advanced visualization, ThoughtSpot and Basedash for plain-English questions on live data, Sigma for warehouse-native analysis, and Domo for connector breadth with unlimited users. The right choice depends on whether you need live warehouse queries, SCIM provisioning, or AI on every plan, since those are the most common gaps teams hit on Zoho Analytics.


### Is Zoho Analytics cheaper than Power BI?


For small teams the two are close. As of October 2026, Zoho Analytics Standard costs $48 per month billed annually for 5 users, or $9.60 per user, while Power BI Pro costs $14 per user per month paid yearly. Zoho includes conversational questions on Standard, while Power BI Copilot requires Fabric F2 or Premium P1 capacity on top of user licenses. Power BI becomes cheaper per head for Microsoft 365 E5 customers, who already have Pro included.


### Zoho Analytics vs Tableau: which is better for a small business?


Zoho Analytics costs far less. Its Premium plan is $115 per month billed annually for 15 users, while 15 Tableau Creator licenses on Tableau Cloud Standard cost $1,125 per month, billed annually. Tableau offers deeper visualization control, a larger analyst community, and SCIM. Zoho Analytics includes an AI agent on Premium, native Zoho app connectors, and anomaly detection on every plan. Most small businesses without a dedicated analyst get more from Zoho Analytics or a lighter alternative.


### Which BI tools let non-technical users query data without SQL?


ThoughtSpot Spotter, Basedash’s AI data analyst, Metabase’s Metabot, Sigma Assistant, Domo AI Chat, and Data Studio Conversational Analytics all answer plain-English questions as of October 2026. They differ on gating: Metabot and Basedash AI chat are on every plan, Spotter starts on ThoughtSpot Pro with 25 queries per user per month, Sigma Assistant needs an AI provider configured by an admin, and Power BI Copilot needs Fabric capacity. Zoho Analytics offers conversational analytics on Standard and its Ask Zia agent on Premium.


### Does Zoho Analytics support live connections to Snowflake or BigQuery?


Yes, on Premium and Enterprise plans. Zoho’s Live Connect documentation says it is “exclusively available for Premium and Enterprise plans,” and it covers PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, and Databricks. Live queries time out after 2.5 minutes by default, and custom queries are not supported in Live Connect. On Basic and Standard, warehouse data is imported and refreshed on a schedule. Alternatives such as Metabase, Sigma, ThoughtSpot, and Basedash query live on every plan.


### Which Zoho Analytics alternatives support SSO and SCIM?


As of October 2026, Tableau, Domo, Sigma, ThoughtSpot, Metabase Pro and Enterprise, and Basedash Enterprise document both SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. Power BI manages users through Microsoft Entra ID. Data Studio uses Google accounts and does not document SAML or SCIM. Zoho Analytics supports SAML 2.0 through Zoho Directory, but its documentation does not describe SCIM for Zoho Analytics itself, which is a common reason IT teams start an evaluation.


### Can I self-host a Zoho Analytics alternative?


Yes. Metabase is open source and self-hostable for free, with paid Pro and Enterprise licenses for features such as SSO and row-level security. Power BI Report Server, Tableau Server, and ThoughtSpot Software run on-premises under enterprise licensing, and Basedash offers self-hosting on its Enterprise plan. Data Studio, Sigma, and Domo are cloud only. Zoho Analytics itself offers an on-premises edition at $30 per user per month billed annually, with a 5-user minimum.
